0:
acl url_discovery path /.well-known/caldav /.well-known/carddav
http-request redirect location /remote.php/dav/ code 301 if url_discovery
option http-keep-alive
timeout server 120000ms

1:
ops=(
  "db:add-missing-primary-keys"
  "db:add-missing-indices"
  "db:add-missing-columns"
  "files:cleanup"
)
grey="\e[1;30m"
reset="\e[0m"
green="\e[1;32m"
red="\e[1;31m"
for op in "$${ops[@]}" ; do
  echo -e "$${grey}Running php occ $op $reset"
  su www-data -s /usr/local/bin/php -- occ $op && echo -en "$green" || echo -en "$red"
  echo -e "Finished php occ $op $reset"
done &&
echo -e "$${grey}Running php occ maintenance:repair --include-expensive $reset"
su www-data -s /usr/local/bin/php -- occ maintenance:repair --include-expensive && echo -en "$green" || echo -en "$red"
echo -e "Finished php occ maintenance:repair --include-expensive $reset"
while :; do /cron.sh; done

chmod +x /var/www/html/custom_apps/notify_push/bin/x86_64/notify_push && \
while :; do su www-data \
  -s /var/www/html/custom_apps/notify_push/bin/x86_64/notify_push -- \
  /var/www/html/config/config.php; sleep 1; done &
pid=$!
grey="\e[1;30m"
reset="\e[0m"
green="\e[1;32m"
red="\e[1;31m"
echo -e "$${grey}Waiting a few seconds for services to start$${reset}"
sleep 10
echo -e "$${grey}Testing if push app is configured"
op="notify_push:setup https://cloud.${personal_domain}/push"
while ! su www-data -s /usr/local/bin/php -- occ "notify_push:self-test"; do
  echo -e "$${grey}Self-test failed, running php occ $op $reset"
  if ! su www-data -s /usr/local/bin/php -- occ $op; then
    echo -e "$${red}$${op} operation failed, retrying...$${reset}"
    sleep 5
  fi
done
echo -e "$${green}Test passed$${reset}"
wait $pid

0: until nc -w 1 -v $POSTGRES_HOST:5432; do echo "Waiting for database"; done

/hr/registry.k8s.io-ingress-nginx-charts.title: ingress-nginx helm release
/hr/registry.k8s.io-ingress-nginx-charts.name: ingress-nginx
/hr/registry.k8s.io-ingress-nginx-charts.doc: ingress-nginx is a popular Kubernetes Ingress controller that provides external access to your applications running in a cluster. It acts as a reverse proxy and load balancer, routing incoming requests to the appropriate backend service based on URL paths and host names. With ingress-nginx, you can easily expose your home lab applications to the internet, allowing you to access them from anywhere with a web browser. Whether you're looking to run a web-based service, host a personal website, or simply want to provide remote access to your applications, ingress-nginx provides a simple and flexible solution for managing external access to your cluster.
